authentication.name: STANDS4 API Credentials
authentication.description: Authenticate requests with the STANDS4 API user id and developer token id.
authentication.notes: The STANDS4 Abbreviations API requires `uid` and `tokenid` query parameters on each request. Do not use bearer authorization for this API.

credentials.name: Developer Token ID

steps.title: Copy the developer token id
steps.description: Copy the value STANDS4 labels as the valid developer token id or `tokenid`.

steps.title: Paste both values into MindCloud
steps.description: Enter `uid` in API User ID and `tokenid` in Developer Token ID.

name: Abbyy
description: Use ABBYY Cloud OCR SDK to submit OCR jobs, inspect processing tasks, and retrieve recognition results from ABBYY's cloud OCR API.

authentication.name: Basic Authentication

setupGuide.title: Set up ABBYY Cloud OCR SDK credentials
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an ABBYY Cloud OCR SDK account and permission to create or view an application in the ABBYY OCR SDK Console.

steps.title: Open the ABBYY OCR SDK Console dashboard
steps.description: Sign in to the ABBYY OCR SDK Console so you can create or review your Cloud OCR SDK applications.

steps.title: Create a new application if you do not already have one
steps.description: Use the Dashboard tab and select '+ Add new application'. When ABBYY asks for a processing location, choose the region your app should use. ABBYY documents that this choice is permanent for the application.

steps.title: Copy the Application ID and Application Password
steps.description: ABBYY sends the Application ID and Application Password in the application-creation email. Enter the Application ID into MindCloud's Username field and the Application Password into MindCloud's Password field.

steps.title: Use the matching processing host for your application region
steps.description: If your ABBYY application was created for the United States processing location, the processing host is https://cloud-westus.ocrsdk.com. Use the processing location that matches the application you created.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Ablefy API credentials

steps.title: Open the ablefy API page in your Ablefy seller account

steps.title: Generate your API credentials
steps.description: Click Generate API key. Ablefy creates two separate credentials for this integration.

steps.title: Copy both values
steps.description: Copy the API key and the Secret Key and store them somewhere secure. Ablefy states that both strings are required for authentication and should be kept secret.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Return to this connection setup. Paste the API key into the API key field. Paste the Secret Key into the Secret field.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate requests to Abstract Public Holidays with an API key.
authentication.notes: Abstract requires the Public Holidays API key in the `api_key` query parameter. The primary credential is platform-managed as `{{credentials.apiKey}}`; do not paste raw API keys into app configuration.

setupGuide.title: Connect Abstract Holidays
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use the API key for Abstract's Public Holidays API. Abstract issues separate keys for each API, so keys from other Abstract products will not work here.

steps.title: Open Abstract Public Holidays
steps.description: Sign in to Abstract and open the Public Holidays API page or dashboard.

steps.title: Copy the Public Holidays API key
steps.description: Copy the API key shown for the Public Holidays API. Do not use a key from another Abstract API product.

steps.title: Create the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Paste the Public Holidays API key into the API key field for this app's connection.

steps.title: Test a holiday lookup
steps.description: Use country `US` and year `2026` to confirm the connection can retrieve holidays.

actions.name: Get Holidays
actions.description: Retrieves holidays from Abstract Holidays for a country and date.

arguments.name: Country
arguments.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as US or SG.

arguments.name: Year
arguments.description: Four-digit year to retrieve holidays for. Required for Abstract free-plan connections and for month/day queries; paid plans may support defaulting for broader lookups.

arguments.name: Month
arguments.description: Month to retrieve, formatted as 01-12. Required for Abstract free-plan individual-day lookups and whenever Day is provided.

arguments.name: Day
arguments.description: Day of month to retrieve, formatted as 01-31. Use with Year and Month for the current verified free-plan lookup path.

setupGuide.title: Connect actiTIME with Basic Auth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need your actiTIME workspace URL and the username and password you use to sign in to actiTIME.

steps.title: Find your workspace URL
steps.description: Open your actiTIME workspace in the browser. Enter the full workspace URL in the Instance URL field without adding /api/v1. For example, if your workspace is https://online.actitime.com/mindcloud, enter exactly that URL.

steps.title: Use your actiTIME sign-in username
steps.description: Enter the same username or email address you use to sign in to actiTIME in the Username field for this connection.

steps.title: Use your actiTIME sign-in password
steps.description: Enter the same password you use to sign in to actiTIME in the Password field for this connection. Do not add any Basic prefix or extra formatting.

steps.title: Save and test the connection
steps.description: After you fill in Instance URL, Username, and Password, save the connection and run the connection test. actiTIME should authorize the request with the same credentials you use in the product.

setupGuide.title: Connect Airmeet custom auth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Airmeet community dashboard and permission to generate API keys from the Integrations tab.

steps.title: Open the Airmeet API key screen
steps.description: Sign in to Airmeet, open your community dashboard, then go to Integrations > API Access Key.

steps.title: Generate a new key pair
steps.description: Click Generate access key and give the key a label you will recognize later.

steps.title: Save the Access Key in MindCloud
steps.description: Copy the X-Airmeet-Access-Key value from Airmeet and paste it into the Access Key field in your Airmeet connection.

steps.title: Save the Secret Key in MindCloud
steps.description: Copy the matching X-Airmeet-Secret-Key value from Airmeet and paste it into the Secret Key field in your Airmeet connection.

steps.title: Generate and store an access token
steps.description: Use the Airmeet Obtain access token action after saving the key pair, then paste the returned token into the Access Token field in the same connection.

name: Airslate
description: Airslate is a document workflow automation platform for organizations to create, send, manage, and track document-driven workflows.

authentication.name: OAuth2 Authorization Code
authentication.description: Authenticate against Airslate using the documented OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow.
authentication.notes: Airslate for this tenant uses the OAuth2 authorization-code flow, not password grant. Authorize URL: https://oauth.airslate.com/public/authorize. Token URL: https://oauth.airslate.com/public/oauth/token. Redirect URI: http://127.0.0.1.

setupGuide.title: How to set up your connection?
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an airSlate DevHub application with a Client ID and Client Secret. This connection uses OAuth2 code grant. In your airSlate app settings, the allowed redirect URI must exactly match `https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/airslate/callback`.

steps.title: Open your airSlate application in DevHub
steps.description: In airSlate DevHub, open the application you created for this integration and go to its application settings.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI to the MindCloud callback
steps.description: Add `https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/airslate/callback` as the redirect URI exactly. A bare host such as `http://127.0.0.1` will not work because airSlate validates the full callback URL.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the connection form
steps.description: Paste the values exactly as shown in DevHub.

steps.title: Use the Connect button to sign in

setupGuide.title: Create an Airtable personal access token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Airtable user API keys no longer work for the Airtable API. For individual API access, Airtable requires a personal access token.

steps.title: Open Airtable's developer hub
steps.description: Open Airtable's developer hub, then go to Personal access tokens under the Developers section.

steps.title: Create the token and choose scopes
steps.description: Click Create token, give the token a name, and add the scopes your Airtable workflows need.

steps.title: Choose which resources the token can access
steps.description: Use Add all resources or Add a base to choose which bases or workspaces the token can reach.

steps.title: Use the new token in MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the Airtable personal access token into the API key field for this connection.

steps.title: Set the access level for each resource
steps.description: For each selected base or workspace, choose the access level Airtable should grant to the integration.

steps.title: Authorize the integration
steps.description: Click Authorize in Airtable to finish the OAuth flow.

setupGuide.title: Connect AlgoDocs
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an AlgoDocs account and a current secret API key from your AlgoDocs dashboard.

steps.title: Open the Rest API settings page in AlgoDocs
steps.description: Sign in to your AlgoDocs account, then open the Rest API settings page where AlgoDocs shows your current secret API key.

steps.title: Copy the current API key

steps.title: Create or edit the AlgoDocs connection in MindCloud
steps.description: In MindCloud, open the AlgoDocs connection and paste the copied key into the API Key field, then save the connection.

name: Algolia

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate with Algolia application ID and API key headers.

credentials.name: Application ID
credentials.description: Your Algolia application ID.

setupGuide.title: Connect Algolia with an Application ID and API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need your Algolia Application ID and an Admin API key. Algolia’s API key docs say main API keys are managed in the dashboard, and the List API keys endpoint requires an Admin API key.

steps.title: Sign in to the Algolia dashboard
steps.description: Open your Algolia account in the dashboard so you can access your application settings and API keys.

steps.title: Open the API keys area for your application
steps.description: Algolia’s API key guide says you can view and manage your main API keys from the dashboard.

steps.title: Copy your Application ID and an Admin API key
steps.description: Use the Application ID for the connection’s Application ID field. Use an Admin API key for the API Key field so the initial List API keys action can run.

actions.name: Get Order Metrics
actions.description: Retrieves order metrics from Amazon Seller.

arguments.name: Marketplace IDs
arguments.description: A marketplace identifier. Specifies the marketplace where the product would be stored.

arguments.name: Interval
arguments.description:
A time interval used for selecting order metrics.

This takes the form of two dates separated by two hyphens (first date is inclusive; second date is exclusive). Dates are in ISO8601 format and must represent absolute time (either Z notation or offset notation).

Example:
- `2018-09-01T00:00:00-07:00--2018-09-04T00:00:00-07:00` requests order metrics for Sept 1st, 2nd and 3rd in the -07:00 zone.

arguments.name: Granularity
arguments.description:
The granularity of the grouping of order metrics, based on a unit of time. Specifying granularity=Hour results in a successful request only if the interval specified is less than or equal to 30 days from now. For all other granularities, the interval specified must be less or equal to 2 years from now. Specifying granularity=Total results in order metrics that are aggregated over the entire interval that you specify. If the interval start and end date don’t align with the specified granularity, the head and tail end of the response interval will contain partial data. Example: Day to get a daily breakdown of the request interval, where the day boundary is defined by the granularityTimeZone.


Month

arguments.name: Granularity Time Zone
arguments.description: An IANA-compatible time zone for determining the day boundary. Required when specifying a granularity value greater than Hour. The granularityTimeZone value must align with the offset of the specified interval value. For example, if the interval value uses Z notation, then granularityTimeZone must be UTC. If the interval value uses an offset, then granularityTimeZone must be an IANA-compatible time zone that matches the offset. Example: US/Pacific to compute day boundaries, accounting for daylight time savings, for US/Pacific zone.

arguments.name: ASIN
arguments.description:
Filters the results by the ASIN that you specify. Specifying both ASIN and SKU returns an error. Do not include this filter if you want the response to include order metrics for all ASINs.

Example:
- `B0792R1RSN`, if you want the response to include order metrics for only ASIN B0792R1RSN.

arguments.name: SKU
arguments.description: Filters the results by the SKU that you specify. Specifying both ASIN and SKU returns an error. Do not include this filter if you want the response to include order metrics for all SKUs. Example: TestSKU, if you want the response to include order metrics for only SKU TestSKU.

arguments.name: Buyer Type
arguments.description:
Filters the results by the buyer type that you specify, B2B (business to business) or B2C (business to customer).

Example:
- `B2B`, if you want the response to include order metrics for only B2B buyers.

arguments.name: Fulfillment Network

Example:
- AFN, if you want the response to include order metrics for only Amazon fulfillment network.

arguments.name: First Day of Week
arguments.description:

Default: `Monday`.

Example:

name: AnnounceKit
description: AnnounceKit is a product communication platform for changelogs, announcements, in-app widgets, feedback, and related product updates. This connector wraps AnnounceKit's documented GraphQL API.

authentication.name: Basic Authentication
authentication.description: Authenticate AnnounceKit GraphQL API requests with HTTP Basic Authentication. Enter the raw AnnounceKit dashboard username/email and password in the connection fields; MindCloud will build the Authorization header.
authentication.notes: AnnounceKit's GraphQL API docs allow Basic Authentication header credentials or dashboard login cookies. Google OAuth login credentials are not valid Basic Auth credentials. For this connector, use an AnnounceKit account that has a local email/password login, set a password for the OAuth email if AnnounceKit supports it, or ask AnnounceKit support for the API Basic Auth credential/token for OAuth-only accounts. Do not enter Google OAuth tokens or Google passwords.

setupGuide.title: Connect AnnounceKit
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an AnnounceKit account with access to the project you want to manage. AnnounceKit's GraphQL API requires HTTP Basic Authentication for API requests unless you are using dashboard login cookies in GraphiQL.

steps.title: Check your login method
steps.description: If you sign in to AnnounceKit only with Google OAuth, those Google credentials are not Basic Auth credentials for the GraphQL API.

steps.title: Prepare API-capable credentials
steps.description: Use an AnnounceKit account with a local email/password login, set a password for the same AnnounceKit email if the dashboard supports it, or contact AnnounceKit support for the Basic Auth credential/token to use with OAuth-only accounts.

steps.title: Enter Basic Auth credentials
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form, enter the raw AnnounceKit username or email in Username and the matching AnnounceKit password or provider-confirmed Basic Auth credential in Password. Do not paste a value starting with Basic unless the connector has been changed to custom Authorization-header auth.

name: AnyDB
description: Manage AnyDB teams, databases, records, shares, and webhooks through AnyDB's external integration API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate with an AnyDB API key plus the email address associated with that key.

credentials.name: Email
credentials.description: The email address for the AnyDB account that owns the API key.

setupGuide.title: Connect your AnyDB account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an AnyDB API key and the corresponding account email before you connect MindCloud.

steps.title: Get your AnyDB API key
steps.description: Open your AnyDB profile dialog and copy the API integration key for the user who will connect MindCloud. The official AnyDB integration docs say the API key is retrieved from the profile dialog.

steps.title: Enter the API key and account email
steps.description: In the MindCloud AnyDB connection form, paste the API key and enter the same email address used for that AnyDB account. The current AnyDB OpenAPI contract requires both x-anydb-api-key and x-anydb-email on authenticated requests.

steps.title: Run the connection test
steps.description: Run the AnyDB connection test to call Validate API Key And Email.

name: Apollo
description: Apollo: Find prospects, enrich contacts, and automate sales outreach

setupGuide.title: Connect Apollo OAuth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Apollo account that can authorize third-party apps/integrations via OAuth. On Apollo plans without custom permission profiles, use an Admin or Billing and Seat Manager account.

steps.title: Start the Apollo connection in MindCloud
steps.description: In MindCloud, open the Apollo connection once so you can copy the redirect URL that MindCloud expects for Apollo OAuth.

steps.title: Register your Apollo integration
steps.description: In Apollo, go to Settings > Integrations, find API, click Connect, then choose OAuth registration. Enter your app name and logo, paste the MindCloud redirect URL, keep an HTTPS callback, and submit.

steps.title: Keep the required scopes enabled
steps.description: Apollo automatically adds read_user_profile and app_scopes. For this Apollo baseline, also keep contacts_search and person_read selected so MindCloud can complete the initial OAuth read action.

steps.title: Finish the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from Apollo into the MindCloud Apollo connection, continue the Connect flow, and approve access in Apollo.

actions.description: Retrieves enriched data for up to 10 people from Apollo.

arguments.name: Run Waterfall Email
arguments.description: Set to true to enable email waterfall enrichment

arguments.name: Run Waterfall Phone
arguments.description: Set to true to enable phone waterfall enrichment

arguments.name: Reveal Personal Emails
arguments.description: Set to `true` if you want to enrich all matched people with personal emails. This potentially consumes credits as part of your Apollo pricing plan . The default value is `false`. If a person resides in a GDPR -compliant region, Apollo will not reveal their personal email.

arguments.name: Reveal Phone Number
arguments.description: Set to `true` if you want to enrich the data of all matched people with all available phone numbers, including mobile phone numbers. This potentially consumes credits as part of your Apollo pricing plan . The default value is `false`. If this parameter is set to `true`, you must enter a webhook URL for the `webhook_url` parameter. Apollo will asynchronously verify phone numbers for you, then send a JSON response that includes only details about the phone numbers to the webhook URL you provide. It can take several minutes for the phone numbers to be delivered.

arguments.name: Webhook URL
arguments.description: If you set the `reveal_phone_number` parameter to `true`, this parameter becomes mandatory. Otherwise, do not use this parameter. Enter the webhook URL that specifies where Apollo should send a JSON response that includes the phone number you requested. Apollo suggests testing this flow to ensure you receive the separate response with the phone number. If phone numbers are not revealed delivered to the webhook URL, try applying UTF-8 encoding to the webhook URL. Example: `https://webhook.site/cc4cf44e-e047-4774-8dac-473d28474e40`; `https%3A%2F%2Fwebhook.site%2Fcc4cf44e-e047-4774-8dac-473d28474e40`

arguments.description: Provide info for each person you want to enrich as an object within this array. Add up to 10 people.

arguments.name: Name
arguments.description: The full name of the person. This will typically be a first name and last name separated by a space. If you use this parameter, you do not need to use the `first_name` and `last_name` parameters. Example: `tim zheng`

arguments.name: Email
arguments.description: The email address of the person. Example: `example@email.com`

arguments.name: Hashed Email

actions.name: Organization Search
actions.description: Finds organizations in Apollo by search criteria.

arguments.name: Q Organization Domains List
arguments.description: The domain name for the person's employer. This can be the current employer or a previous employer. Do not include `www.`, the `@` symbol, or similar. This parameter accepts up to 1,000 domains in a single request. Examples: `apollo.io`; `microsoft.com`

arguments.name: Organization Num Employees Ranges
arguments.description: The number range of employees working for the company. This enables you to find companies based on headcount. You can add multiple ranges to expand your search results. Each range you add needs to be a string, with the upper and lower numbers of the range separated only by a comma. Examples: `1,10`; `250,500`; `10000,20000`

arguments.name: Organization Locations
arguments.description: The location of the company headquarters. You can search across cities, US states, and countries. If a company has several office locations, results are still based on the headquarters location. For example, if you search `chicago` but a company's HQ location is in `boston`, any Boston-based companies will not appearch in your search results, even if they match other parameters.. To exclude companies based on location, use the `organization_not_locations` parameter. Examples: `texas`; `tokyo`; `spain`

arguments.name: Organization Not Locations
arguments.description: Exclude companies from search results based on the location of the company headquarters. You can use cities, US states, and countries as locations to exclude. This parameter is useful for ensuring you do not prospect in an undesirable territory. For example, if you use `ireland` as a value, no Ireland-based companies will appear in your search results. Examples: `minnesota`; `ireland`; `seoul`

arguments.name: Revenue Range[min]
arguments.description: Search for organizations based on their revenue. Use this parameter to set the lower range of organization revenue. Use the `revenue_range[max]` parameter to set the upper range of revenue. Do not enter currency symbols, commas, or decimal points in the figure. Example: `300000`

arguments.name: Revenue Range[max]
arguments.description: Search for organizations based on their revenue. Use this parameter to set the upper range of organization revenue. Use the `revenue_range[min]` parameter to set the lower range of revenue. Do not enter currency symbols, commas, or decimal points in the figure. Example: `50000000`

arguments.name: Currently Using Any Of Technology Uids
arguments.description: Find organizations based on the technologies they currently use. Apollo supports filtering by 1,500+ technologies. Apollo calculates technologies data from multiple sources. This data is updated regularly. Check out the full list of supported technologies by downloading this CSV file . Use underscores (`_`) to replace spaces and periods for the technologies listed in the CSV file. Examples: `salesforce`; `google_analytics`; `wordpress_org`

arguments.name: Q Organization Keyword Tags
arguments.description: Filter search results based on keywords associated with companies. For example, you can enter `mining` as a value to return only companies that have an association with the mining industry. Examples: `mining`; `sales strategy`; `consulting`

arguments.name: Q Organization Name
arguments.description: Filter search results to include a specific company name. If the value you enter for this parameter does not match with a company's name, the company will not appear in search results, even if it matches other parameters. Partial matches are accepted. For example, if you filter by the value `marketing`, a company called `NY Marketing Unlimited` would still be eligible as a search result, but `NY Market Analysis` would not be eligible. Example: `apollo` or `mining`

arguments.name: Organization Ids
arguments.description: The Apollo IDs for the companies you want to include in your search results. Each company in the Apollo database is assigned a unique ID. To find IDs, identify the values for `organization_id` when you call this endpoint. Example: `5e66b6381e05b4008c8331b8`

arguments.name: Latest Funding Amount Range[min]

Do not enter currency symbols, commas, or decimal points in the figure. Examples: `5000000`; `15000000`

actions.name: Search for Accounts
actions.description: Finds accounts in your Apollo account.

arguments.name: Q Organization Name
arguments.description: Add keywords to narrow the search of the accounts in your team's Apollo account. Keywords should directly match at least part of an account's name. For example, searching the keyword `marketing` might return the result `NY Marketing Unlimited`, but not `NY Market Analysts`. This parameter only searches account names, not other account fields. Examples: `apollo`; `microsoft`; `marketing`

arguments.name: Account Stage Ids
arguments.description: The Apollo IDs for the account stages that you want to include in your search results. If you add multiple account stages, Apollo will include all accounts that match any of the stages, along with the other parameters, in the search results. Call the [List Account Stages endpoint](https://docs.apollo.io/reference/list-account-stages) to retrieve a list of all the account stage IDs available in your Apollo account. Example: `61b8e913e0f4d2012e3af74e`

arguments.name: Account Label Ids
arguments.description: The Apollo IDs for the labels that you want to include in your search results. If you add multiple labels, Apollo will include all accounts connected to any of the labels, along with the other parameters, in the search results. Example: `['6095a710bd01d100a506d4ae']`

arguments.name: Sort By Field
arguments.description: Sort the matching accounts by 1 of the following options: - `account_last_activity_date`: The most recent activity date recorded first. - `account_created_at`: The most recently created first. - `account_updated_at`: The most recently updated first.

arguments.name: Sort Ascending
arguments.description: Set to `true` to sort the matching accounts in ascending order. This parameter must be used with `sort_by_field`. Otherwise, the sorting logic is not applied. Example: `true`

actions.description: Finds outreach emails in your Apollo account.

arguments.name: Emailer Message Stats
arguments.description: Find emails based on their current status, such as whether they were delivered or opened. You can add multiple statuses. Possible values include: `delivered` `scheduled` `drafted` `not_opened` `opened` `clicked` `unsubscribed` `demoed` `bounced` `spam_blocked` `failed_other`

arguments.name: Emailer Message Reply Classes
arguments.description: Find emails based on the response sentiment of the recipient. This can include the recipient expressing interest in meeting or having a follow-up question. You can add multiple values. Possible values include: `willing_to_meet` `follow_up_question` `person_referral` `out_of_office` `already_left_company_or_not_right_person` `not_interested` `unsubscribe` `none_of_the_above`

arguments.name: User Ids
arguments.description: Find emails sent by specific users in your team's Apollo account. You can add multiple users. Use the Get a List of Users endpoint to retrieve IDs for all of the users within your Apollo account. Example: `66302798d03b9601c7934ebf`

arguments.name: Emailer Campaign Ids
arguments.description: Search for emails that are included in specific sequences in your Apollo account. You can search multiple sequences. arguments.name: Not Emailer Campaign Ids
arguments.description: Exclude emails from specific sequences in your Apollo account. You can exclude multiple sequences. steps.description: During AppFit setup, choose the right Industry, Platform, and Focus for your company so AppFit can suggest the metrics you should track.

steps.title: Use your AppFit API key
steps.description: AppFit’s official integration snippet initializes the SDK with window.startAppFit("API_KEY"), so the connection should use that same AppFit API key value.

steps.title: Save the connection and send a test event
steps.description: After saving the connection, run the AppFit action and confirm AppFit begins receiving event data and updating metrics.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect AppFollow with an API token from the AppFollow API Dashboard.

setupGuide.title: Get your AppFollow API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an AppFollow account with Account Owner or Admin access.

steps.title: Open the API Dashboard

steps.title: Create or copy an API token

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: In the AppFollow connection form, paste the token into the API Key field and save the connection.

steps.description: Use the matching API password for the same ApptiveGrid account or workspace.

name: Apptoto
description: Manage appointments, contacts, bookings, and reminder messages

setupGuide.title: Get your Apptoto API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an active Apptoto account with access to Settings > Integrations.

steps.title: Sign in to Apptoto
steps.description: Use the Apptoto account you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Open Developer Tools
steps.description: In Apptoto, go to Settings > Integrations and open the Developer Tools section.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.description: Click API Keys, choose Add API Key, enter a name for the key, and create it.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the generated API key and keep it private. You will paste this value into MindCloud immediately.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Back in MindCloud, set Username to your Apptoto email or username and set Password to the API key you just created.

setupGuide.title: Get your Appzi portal token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Appzi Portal for the portal you want to connect.

steps.title: Sign in to the Appzi Portal
steps.description: Open the Appzi Portal and sign in to the account that owns the portal you want to connect.

steps.title: Choose the correct portal
steps.description: If your account has more than one portal, open the portal whose surveys you want MindCloud to read.

steps.title: Open Portal Settings
steps.description: In the Appzi Portal, go to Settings and then Portal Settings.

steps.title: Copy the portal token
steps.description: In the Installation Code section, copy only the token value used in the Appzi script URL or the window.appziSettings.portal value.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the copied value into the Portal Token field for this connection.

name: ARForms
description: Receive ARForms form submissions through custom webhooks

authentication.name: No authentication
authentication.description: ARForms sends form submissions to a MindCloud-generated webhook URL without provider credentials.

setupGuide.title: Connect ARForms with a webhook URL
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a MindCloud workflow step that exposes an ARForms webhook URL, plus admin access to the WordPress site running ARForms.

steps.title: Copy the MindCloud webhook URL
steps.description: In MindCloud, open the workflow step that uses the ARForms trigger and copy its unique webhook URL.

steps.title: Open the ARForms form
steps.description: In WordPress admin, edit the form that should send submissions to MindCloud.

steps.title: Open Submit Action settings
steps.description: In the form editor, click Submit Action from the top belt.

steps.title: Enable the custom webhook option
steps.description: Turn on “Send Form data internally to custom URL (webhook)” and paste the MindCloud webhook URL into the custom URL field.

steps.title: Save the form and send a test submission
steps.description: Save the ARForms form, submit a test entry from the form, then confirm the workflow trigger receives the payload in MindCloud.

setupGuide.title: Create an Arize AX service key

steps.title: Open the API Keys page in Arize AX
steps.description: In Arize AX, open Settings from the left navigation and then open API Keys.

steps.title: Copy the current Space ID
steps.description: On the API Keys page, copy the value shown in the Current SpaceID box. You will paste this into the MindCloud connection as Space ID.

steps.title: Create a new Service Key
steps.description: Select + New API Key, enter a name, and choose Service Key as the key type.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use an Ascora Auth key generated in Administration > API Settings.

setupGuide.title: Get your Ascora API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Ascora account with Full Administration rights.

steps.title: Sign in to Ascora Admin
steps.description: Open the Ascora admin login and sign in with a user that has Full Administration rights.

steps.title: Open API Settings
steps.description: In the Ascora Dashboard, click Administration. Under Settings, click API Settings.

steps.title: Generate and copy your API key
steps.description: Click Generate New API Key if there is no key yet, then click Copy to Clipboard. Keep the key somewhere secure because you will need it when connecting Ascora to MindCloud.

name: Aspera on Cloud
description: REST API for IBM Aspera on Cloud files, packages, workspaces, users, and admin resources.

authentication.name: JWT Bearer (OAuth2)
authentication.description: Aspera on Cloud OAuth2 JWT bearer token exchange.
authentication.notes: Use the Aspera API client ID, client secret, API user email, and RSA private key that matches the public key registered in Aspera on Cloud. The runtime now exchanges a signed JWT bearer assertion for an access token. Redirect URI and subscription ID are not used in the documented bearer-token request itself.

credentials.name: Client ID
credentials.description: Aspera API client ID.

credentials.name: API User Email
credentials.description: Email address used as the JWT subject claim.

credentials.name: Scope
credentials.description: Requested Aspera API scope, typically user:all.

credentials.name: Tenant URL
credentials.description: Optional Aspera tenant URL used to derive the organization-specific token endpoint.

setupGuide.title: Connect Aspera on Cloud
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Aspera on Cloud API client, an API user email, and the RSA private key that matches the public key registered for that API user.

steps.title: Open your Aspera on Cloud tenant
steps.description: Sign in to your Aspera on Cloud organization with an administrator account.

steps.title: Create or open an API client
steps.description: In Aspera on Cloud, go to the API client area and create a client for MindCloud, or open the client you already created for this integration.

steps.title: Register the callback URL
steps.description: Add the MindCloud callback URL that you registered during provider setup to the API client redirect URIs and save the client.

steps.title: Enable JWT authentication for the API client
steps.description: Turn on JWT authentication for the API client and attach the public key that matches the private key you will store in MindCloud.

steps.title: Verify the API user public key
steps.description: Make sure the API user account you will authenticate as has the matching public key on its profile.

steps.title: Enter the connection fields in MindCloud
steps.description: Use the client ID, client secret, API user email, private key PEM, and scope when creating the MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Create a new Aspire credential

actions.name: Approve Receipt
actions.description: Approves an existing Aspire receipt and can optionally receive it at the same time. This is the only post-create update path for a receipt. At approve time, the only receipt fields that can be added or changed are the vendor invoice number and vendor invoice date. No other receipt field can be edited through this action, including notes, extra costs or freight, receipt items, received date, vendor, branch, or work ticket. If the user asks to change a non-invoice-metadata field on an existing receipt, surface that limitation upfront and offer the available path of recreating the receipt with the corrected values.

actions.name: Receive Receipt
actions.description: Marks an existing Aspire receipt as received. This action accepts the receipt identifier only and does not perform receipt-level edits. It cannot set or change invoice metadata, notes, extra costs or freight, receipt items, received date, or any other receipt field. If the user wants to record vendor invoice number or vendor invoice date around the same workflow, use approveReceipt because approveReceipt is the only post-create path for those two fields. For any other requested change to an existing receipt, explain that Aspire has no updateReceipt or patch action and the receipt must be recreated with the correct values.

name: AssessTEAM
description: Manage employee evaluations, goals, OKRs, and performance reports

authentication.name: API Key Token Flow
authentication.description: Use an AssessTEAM API key and company name to mint a bearer token before running actions.

credentials.name: API Key
credentials.description: AssessTEAM API key from Settings -> Integrations -> Application Programming Interface.

credentials.name: Company Name
credentials.description: AssessTEAM workspace subdomain / company name used by the token endpoint.

setupGuide.title: Connect AssessTEAM with API key token flow
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the AssessTEAM API key plus the workspace subdomain / company name used by the token endpoint.

steps.title: Sign in as the account owner
steps.description: Open the AssessTEAM login page and sign in with an account owner profile.

steps.title: Open the API settings page
steps.description: In AssessTEAM, go to Settings > Integration > Application Programming Interface.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the API key shown on the page and paste it into the MindCloud connection form as API Key.

steps.title: Enter the workspace subdomain
steps.description: Enter the AssessTEAM workspace subdomain or company name used by the token endpoint, for example mind87766.

setupGuide.title: NASA API key setup
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a NASA API key from api.nasa.gov. NASA also supports DEMO_KEY for limited demo usage, but a personal key is recommended for regular use.

steps.title: Open the NASA API portal
steps.description: Go to the NASA API portal and use the Generate API Key form.

steps.title: Save the key in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the NASA API key into this connection's API key field.

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Astra organization that owns the resources you want to manage. MindCloud uses the unified application token that starts with AstraCS:.

steps.title: Sign in to the Astra Portal
steps.description: Open the Astra Portal in your browser and sign in with an account that can create organization tokens.

steps.title: Open the token management page
steps.description: In Astra Portal, open Settings, make sure the organization filter is set to the correct organization, and then open Tokens.

steps.title: Generate a new application token
steps.description: In Generate New Token, choose the role you want the token to have, optionally add a description and expiration, and then click Generate Token.

steps.title: Copy the AstraCS token
steps.description: Copy the token value that starts with AstraCS:. Astra only shows the full token once, so store it somewhere secure before leaving the page.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: Use the copied AstraCS token as the MindCloud API key for this connection. You do not need to enter the legacy client ID or secret for the DevOps API.

steps.title: Add MindCloud's redirect URL

steps.title: Enable the required scopes

steps.title: Copy the API token

setupGuide.title: Set up Auth0 Management API access
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Auth0 tenant admin account and a machine-to-machine application that is authorized for the Auth0 Management API.

steps.title: Open your Auth0 dashboard
steps.description: Sign in to your Auth0 tenant as an administrator.

steps.title: Create or open a machine-to-machine application
steps.description: In Auth0, create a Machine to Machine Application if you do not already have one for MindCloud.

steps.title: Authorize the Auth0 Management API
steps.description: Authorize your machine-to-machine application for the Auth0 Management API and grant the scopes you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Copy your tenant domain
steps.description: Find your tenant domain, such as your-tenant.us.auth0.com. You will enter this as Tenant Domain in MindCloud.

steps.title: Copy your client credentials
steps.description: From the application settings, copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the MindCloud connection.

name: Authkey

authentication.name: API Key

setupGuide.title: Connect your Authkey account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Authkey account and access to the Authkey console. If the shared apps@mindcloud.co signup is still incomplete, finish the required reCAPTCHA and account creation first.

steps.title: Sign in to the Authkey console
steps.description: Open the Authkey console and log in with the account that owns the API credential you want to use in MindCloud.

steps.title: Open My Account > Profile
steps.description: In the Authkey console, go to My Account, then open Profile. The official docs say your authkey is available there.

steps.title: Copy the authkey
steps.description: Copy the authkey value from the Profile page.

steps.title: Paste the value into the MindCloud connection
steps.description: When MindCloud asks for the API Key, paste the authkey value you copied from Authkey.

name: Autotask
description: Autotask: Manage companies, opportunities, projects, contacts, resources, and attachments

authentication.name: Autotask API Credentials
authentication.description: Authenticate with an Autotask API-only username, secret, and integration code.

credentials.name: Username
credentials.description: Autotask API-only user email.

credentials.name: Secret
credentials.description: Secret for the Autotask API-only user.

credentials.name: API Integration Code
credentials.description: Tracking identifier assigned to this integration.

setupGuide.title: Connect an Autotask API user
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Autotask administrator with HR security access and a dedicated API-only user for this integration.

glossary.definition: A dedicated Autotask account that can use the API but cannot sign in to the Autotask interface.
The tracking identifier assigned to this Autotask integration.

steps.title: Confirm the API-only user
steps.description: Ask an Autotask administrator to create or verify a dedicated resource with an API User (API-only) security level and only the permissions this integration needs.

steps.title: Collect the connection values
steps.description: On the API-only user's Security tab, collect the user name, Secret, and tracking identifier. An HR administrator must provide these because API-only users cannot access the interface.

steps.title: Complete the connection form
steps.description: Enter the API user email in Username, the API account password in Secret, and the tracking identifier in API Integration Code. Then save the connection.

arguments.description: The Autotask company for this opportunity. If Contact ID is provided, the contact must be active and belong to this company or its parent.

setupGuide.title: How to connect Avalara AvaTax
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an Avalara AvaTax account with REST v2 access. This connection uses Basic authentication.

steps.title: Choose your AvaTax environment
steps.description: Use Sandbox for testing or Production for live traffic. In MindCloud, set the Environment field to the matching AvaTax REST base URL.

steps.title: Generate or confirm your Avalara credentials
steps.description: If customers will set up this connector themselves, Avalara recommends Account ID and License Key. Sign in to the AvaTax Website as an account administrator, open Settings, and choose Reset License Key. If your team uses user credentials instead, prepare the username and password for the same environment.

steps.title: Enter the values in MindCloud
steps.description: Select the Environment URL first, then enter your Basic-auth credential pair in the connection form. MindCloud will send those values as a Basic Authorization header to AvaTax REST v2.

steps.title: Run Test Connection
steps.description: Use the Test Connection action after saving the connection. Avalara documents the Ping endpoint as the connectivity check used to verify network reachability and credential recognition.

setupGuide.title: Create an Avaza OAuth app

steps.title: Open Developer Apps
steps.description: Sign in to Avaza and go to Settings > Manage Developer Apps.

steps.title: Create an OAuth app
steps.description: Click Add OAuth App. Enter an app name and description, choose the Server-to-Server client type, and set the redirect URL to https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/avaza/callback.

steps.title: Save and copy the credentials

actions.name: Create Bill
actions.description: Creates a new bill in Avaza.

arguments.name: Transactionprefix
arguments.description: A prefix for the Invoice number. e.g. 'INV'. If left blank it will be set to the account default. Max length 20 characters.

arguments.name: Billnumber
arguments.description: Pass any string. If left blank it will use the next number in the auto incrementing sequence. If an integer is passed then the largest integer will be use as the seed to auto generate the next invoice number in the sequence.

arguments.name: Companyidfk
arguments.description: If left blank then you must specify Company Name.

arguments.name: Companyname
arguments.description: If left blank then you must specify Company ID. Specified Name will be used to match existing customer record. If not matched then it will be used to create a new customer. First Name, Last Name and Email will only be used if it is a new company. If the Company name appears multiple times we will check the email address to find a matching company. If email address doesn't identify a matching company then the invoice creation will be rejected.

arguments.name: Firstname
arguments.description: Specified value will be used to create a new customer contact only if a new customer is being created.

arguments.name: Lastname
arguments.description: Specified value will be used to create a new customer contact only if a new customer is being created.

arguments.name: Email
arguments.description: Specified value will be used to create a new customer contact only if a new customer is being created.

arguments.name: Currencycode
arguments.description: Expects ISO Standard 3 character currency code. If left blank the currency will default to account's currency in general setting. For existing companies this field will be ignored and the invoice will use the currency of the customer. For new customers if the currency is not specified then account currency will be used otherwise the specified currency will be used.

arguments.name: Exchangerate
arguments.description: Exchange rate is only valid for invoices in currency other than default account currency. If not specified it will get the market rate based on the Date Issued.

arguments.name: Billtemplateidfk
arguments.description: If left blank the account default invoice template will be used.

arguments.name: Subject
arguments.description: Plain UTF8 text. (no HTML). 255 characters max

arguments.name: Supplierponumber
arguments.description: Plain UTF8 text. 100 characters max

arguments.name: Dateissued
arguments.description: If not specified it will use today's date. The date should be specified as local date.

arguments.name: Paymentterms
arguments.description:

actions.name: Create Bill Payment
actions.description: Creates a new bill payment in Avaza.

arguments.name: Paymentnumber
arguments.description: Optional. If not specified will be automatically generated

arguments.name: Dateissued
arguments.description: Date of Payment. If not specified, assumes today.

arguments.name: Transactionprefix
arguments.description: Optional to override the default prefix added to Payment Numbers

arguments.name: Companyidfk
arguments.description: Only required if no invoice allocations specified.

arguments.name: Exchangerate
arguments.description: Optional. Only used when the Company's currency is different from the Avaza account's base currency. Specifies the exchange rate that should apply between the Company currency and base currency. If not provided we will obtain an up to date exchange rate for the Payment Issue Date.

arguments.name: Transactionreference
arguments.description: Optional for storing the reference # of the payment method.

arguments.name: Paymentprovidercode
arguments.description: Optional for storing the payment provider who was the source of funds.

arguments.name: Currencycode
arguments.description: Optional for specifying the Bill Payment's Currency (3 letter ISO Currency Code).

arguments.name: Paymentallocations
arguments.description: List of amounts within this payment that are allocated to invoices. The sum of these be less than or equal to the payment amount.

arguments.name: Billtransactionidfk
arguments.description: The Avaza Bill TransactionID that is having a payment amount allocated to it.

arguments.name: Allocationamount
arguments.description: The Amount being allocated to the bill. Expects same currency as bill currency

setupGuide.title: Set up AWeber OAuth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an AWeber developer account and permission to create an OAuth app.

steps.title: Create an AWeber developer app
steps.description: Sign in to AWeber Developer and create an app for this MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.description: From your AWeber app, copy the client ID and client secret into the MindCloud connection form.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.description: In your AWeber app settings, add the exact redirect URI shown in MindCloud. AWeber requires the redirect URI used during authorization to match the redirect URI saved on the app.

steps.title: Authenticate the connection
steps.description: Back in MindCloud, save the client credentials and continue through the AWeber OAuth popup to authorize access.

name: Azure SQL
description: Build, modernize, and scale SQL apps with managed Azure databases.

credentials.name: Client Secret
credentials.description: Required only for Azure Active Directory Service Principal Secret authentication type

setupGuide.title: Set up your Azure SQL connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the Azure SQL server name and database name. Depending on the authentication type you choose, you also need either a SQL username and password or Microsoft Entra service principal credentials.

steps.title: Find the server and database names in Azure
steps.description: In the Azure portal, open the Azure SQL server and database you want MindCloud to use. Note the server name and the database name exactly as Azure shows them.

steps.title: Choose the authentication type you will use
steps.description: Decide whether this connection will use SQL credentials or Microsoft Entra service principal credentials. If you use a service principal, collect the client ID, client secret, and tenant ID before you continue.

steps.title: Enter the core connection fields in MindCloud
steps.description: Enter the Server and Database values in MindCloud. If your environment uses the default Azure SQL port, use 1433. Leave Encrypt enabled unless your database administrator explicitly tells you to use a different setting.

steps.title: Enter the credentials that match your authentication type
steps.description: If you chose SQL authentication, enter the username and password. If you chose the Microsoft Entra service principal option, enter the client ID, client secret, and tenant ID instead.
